mainTopic: Thigh bones of קדשים, נבלה, שרץ and מת: when they make things טמא by touch or by אהל, and whether marrow heals the bone
overview: The משנה finishes its list of hollow thigh bones (קוּלִית). The bone of a disqualified קרבן makes a person טמא whether it is sealed or has a hole. The bones of a נבלה and a שרץ make a person טמא only if they have a hole, and a פסוק teaches that carrying follows the same rule as touching. The גמרא then reads the משנה's word 'touches' about a מת's thigh bone to mean that it does not make things טמא through אהל. It asks what case this could be, ruling out a כזית of flesh, a כזית of marrow, and a bone that counts as a full limb. רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא concludes that, according to the משנה, marrow does not heal the flesh outside. The גמרא splits the משנה's clauses by the amount of marrow and explains what each clause teaches, including רבי יצחק's rule that a bone holding נותר is a בסיס. אביי instead says the bone was scraped, in line with רבי אלעזר. רבי יוחנן says 'touching' includes overhanging, and a משנה in אהלות about joining half-measures is brought as proof. The גמרא then begins to challenge that proof from the end of the same משנה, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Thigh bone of a disqualified offering is impure either way
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who touches the thigh bone of קדשים is טמא, whether the bone is sealed or has a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the thigh bone of sacrificial animals: one who touches them is impure, whether they are sealed or perforated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of thigh bones. It says that touching the thigh bone of a disqualified קרבן makes you טמא no matter what condition the bone is in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here it makes no difference whether the bone is sealed or open. This is the same rule as for the bone of a מת, which is mentioned just before this line. The impurity of these קדשים bones comes from a rabbinic decree, so it does not depend on whether you can reach the marrow.

keyTerms.meaning: The thigh bone, a hollow bone with marrow inside
Sacrificial animals (here, ones that became פִּגּוּל or נוֹתָר)
Sealed, with no opening to the marrow
Perforated, with a hole to the marrow
Ritually impure

phrases.english: And the thigh bone of sacrificial animals,
phrases.notes: The 'and' joins this to the thigh bone of a מת, which the משנה mentioned just before. These are קרבנות that became פיגול or נותר.

phrases.english: one who touches them,
whether sealed or perforated, is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list, which began with the thigh bone of a מת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching the thigh bone of disqualified קדשים makes one טמא, whether the bone is sealed or perforated.

steps.title: Thigh bones of a carcass and a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The thigh bone of a נבלה or a שרץ makes a person טמא only if it has a hole, even a tiny one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The thigh bone of a נבלה and the thigh bone of a שרץ: one who touches them when sealed is pure; if they have any hole at all, they make impure through touching.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a different rule for the bones of a נבלה and a שרץ. Sealed bones are טהור, and bones with a hole make a person טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bones of a נבלה and a שרץ are not טמא on their own. The impurity comes from the marrow inside. If the bone is sealed, touching it does not count as touching the marrow. Once there is even the smallest hole, touching the bone counts as touching the marrow.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
One of the eight creeping creatures that are טמא
Ritually pure
Any amount at all, even the smallest
Contact, impurity passed on by touching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 1. For קדשים, sealed or open makes no difference. For נבלה and שרץ, a sealed bone is completely טהור.

phrases.english: The thigh bone of a carcass and the thigh bone of a creeping animal,
one who touches them when sealed: they are pure,
if perforated even slightly, it makes impure through contact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a contrasting rule for different kinds of bones
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed thigh bone of a נבלה or שרץ is טהור. A perforated one makes impure through touching.

steps.title: Carrying follows the same rule as touching
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a פסוק to show that the sealed-or-perforated rule also applies to carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that this also applies to carrying? The verse says 'one who touches' and 'one who carries.' Whatever is included in impurity through touching is included in impurity through carrying. Whatever is not included in touching is not included in carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks how we know that carrying a sealed bone is also טהור, while carrying a perforated bone makes a person טמא. It answers by pointing to a פסוק that mentions touching and carrying side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists touching a נבלה and carrying a נבלה next to each other. From this the משנה learns that the two always go together. Since a sealed bone does not make a person טמא through touching, it does not make him טמא through carrying either.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying, impurity passed on by lifting or carrying
From where do we know?
The verse comes to teach

steps.whatToRemember: For נבלה and שרץ bones, touching and carrying follow the same rule. If touching does not make a person טמא, carrying does not either.

phrases.english: From where do we know it applies even to carrying?
The verse states: 'One who touches … and one who carries,'

phrases.english: that which enters the category of contact enters the category of carrying,

phrases.english: what does not enter the category of contact does not enter the category of carrying.

steps.title: Inference: touching makes impure, overlying does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's word 'touches' about a מת's thigh bone to mean that overlying it does not make a person טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Touching, yes; but overlying, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a precise reading of the משנה about the thigh bone of a מת. The משנה said 'one who touches,' so the גמרא learns that being over the bone or under the same roof does not make a person טמא. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מת can usually make things טמא through אהל, meaning by being under the same roof. The משנה mentions only touching, which shows that this bone does not make anything טמא through אהל. The גמרא will now ask what kind of case would lead to that result.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Yes
Overlies, being over the item or under the same roof with it

phrases.english: GEMARA:
One who touches: yes,
phrases.notes: This is going back to the start of the משנה, which spoke about the thigh bone of a מת.

phrases.english: but one who overlies: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening case of the משנה (the thigh bone of a מת) and draws a precise reading from it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the wording of the משנה: the thigh bone of a מת makes a person טמא through touching, but not through אהל.

steps.title: What case is this? Flesh would make impure in a tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means. If there were a כזית of flesh on the bone, it should also make things טמא through אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances? If there is an olive-bulk of flesh, it should make impure in a tent as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 4 by asking what case the משנה is talking about. It points out that one possible case does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כזית of flesh from a מת makes things טמא through אהל. If that much flesh were attached to the bone, the משנה would not limit the impurity to touching. So the משנה cannot be talking about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
An olive-bulk, a measure of size
A tent; impurity passed on by being under the same roof
Also, as well

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If there is an olive-bulk of flesh,
phrases.notes: He means flesh of the מת still attached to the bone.

phrases.english: it should make impure in a tent as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי אִי דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 4 by asking what case would fit it
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the thigh bone of a מת does not make impure through אהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a כזית of flesh were on the bone, that flesh alone would make things טמא through אהל, so the 'touching only' reading would be wrong.

steps.title: The case is less than an olive-bulk of flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a bone with less than a כזית of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is not an olive-bulk of flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about a bone that does not have a כזית of flesh on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a כזית of flesh, nothing on the bone makes things טמא through אהל. So the bone makes a person טמא only through touching, which fits the משנה's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: There is not

phrases.english: Where there is not an olive-bulk of flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It might seem the bone could have a כזית of flesh, which would make things טמא through אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a bone with less than a כזית of flesh, so it makes a person טמא only through touching.

steps.title: What if there is a full כזית of marrow inside the bone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if there is a כזית of marrow inside the bone, the טומאה should break out of the bone and spread through אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there is a כזית of marrow inside the bone, the טומאה breaks through and goes up. So it should also make things טמא through אהל!
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 explained that the משנה means a bone with less than a כזית of flesh on it. Now the גמרא asks about the marrow inside the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כזית of flesh from a מת makes things טמא through אהל. A bone around the marrow does not block that טומאה, because the טומאה 'breaks through' the bone and rises. So if the bone holds a כזית of marrow, it should make things טמא through אהל, which contradicts the משנה's limit to touching.

keyTerms.meaning: Marrow, the soft material inside a bone
The טומאה breaks through and goes up, so the bone around it does not hold it in
Becoming טמא by being under the same roof as a מת, or by being over it
An olive's worth, the minimum amount of a מת's flesh that makes things טמא through אהל

phrases.english: But if there is an olive-bulk of marrow inside
the impurity breaks through and goes up
it should make things impure in a tent as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'less than a כזית of flesh' answer of Step 6 and asks about the marrow inside the bone instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule (Step 4) that a מת's thigh bone makes things טמא only by touch and not through אהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כזית of marrow from a מת should make things טמא through אהל, because the bone around it does not block the טומאה.

steps.title: The bone has less than a כזית of marrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means a bone with less than a כזית of marrow inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה means a case where there is not a כזית of marrow inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 7 the same way it answered Step 6. The משנה is talking about a bone with less than a כזית of marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה's case is narrowed twice: less than a כזית of flesh outside the bone and less than a כזית of marrow inside it. With no כזית anywhere, there is nothing to make things טמא through אהל, and only the bone itself makes things טמא by touch.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is not
Inside

phrases.english: Where there is not an olive-bulk of marrow inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bone might hold a כזית of marrow, so it would make things טמא through אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a bone with less than a כזית of marrow, so there is no טומאה through אהל.

steps.title: If marrow regrows flesh, the bone is a full limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if marrow inside a bone can heal and regrow the flesh outside, then the bone counts as a full limb, and it should make things טמא through אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if marrow inside heals the flesh outside, then this is a proper limb. So it should also make things טמא through אהל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the bone, even with less than a כזית of marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full limb (אבר) from a מת makes things טמא through אהל even if it is smaller than a כזית. If the marrow inside could heal and rebuild the flesh, then the bone with its marrow would count as a complete limb. In that case it should make things טמא through אהל, and the משנה says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Heals, makes the flesh grow back
A proper, complete limb
On the outside

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measures. Flesh needs a כזית to make things טמא through אהל, but a complete limb makes things טמא through אהל at any size. That is why calling the bone a 'proper limb' causes a problem even with less than a כזית.

phrases.english: But if marrow inside
heals the flesh outside
phrases.notes: He means that in a living person the marrow helps the flesh around the bone grow back.

phrases.english: it is a proper limb
it should make things impure in a tent as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מוֹחַ מִבִּפְנִים מַעֲלֶה אֲרוּכָה מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that the 'less than a כזית' answer of Step 8 does not solve, because a full limb has no minimum size.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a מת's thigh bone makes things טמא only by touch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the marrow can rebuild the flesh, the bone is a full limb, and a full limb makes things טמא through אהל at any size.

steps.title: The משנה holds that marrow does not regrow flesh
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא concludes from the משנה that marrow inside a bone does not heal the flesh outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, the son of רבי חייא, said: This shows that marrow inside does not heal the flesh outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא answers Step 9 by learning a fact from the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says the bone makes things טמא only by touch and not through אהל. So the משנה must hold that marrow cannot rebuild flesh, and the bone is therefore not a full limb. The words 'זאת אומרת' show that this is an inference from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This shows', an inference drawn from a source
Does not heal, does not make the flesh grow back

steps.whatToRemember: According to the משנה, marrow does not rebuild flesh. So a מת's thigh bone is not a full limb and makes things טמא only by touch.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, says
That is to say

phrases.aramaic: מוֹחַ בִּפְנִים אֵינוֹ מַעֲלֶה אֲרוּכָה מִבַּחוּץ
phrases.english: marrow inside does not heal the flesh outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by drawing a fact about marrow from the משנה's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marrow can rebuild flesh, so the bone would be a full limb that makes things טמא through אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה holds that marrow does not rebuild flesh, so the bone is not a full limb.

steps.title: Then why does a thigh bone of מוקדשים make things טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the משנה means a bone with less than a כזית of marrow, why does the משנה say the thigh bone of מוקדשים makes things טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the משנה? As a case with less than a כזית. If so, why does the bone of מוקדשים make things טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the answer of Step 8, that there is less than a כזית, and attacks it using another part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also says that a thigh bone of מוקדשים makes a person טמא by touch. That rule comes from a rabbinic decree about bones attached to פיגול or נותר. פיגול and נותר need a כזית. If there is less than a כזית of marrow, there is no פיגול or נותר, so why would the bone make anyone טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) the case?
If so
Animals set aside as קרבנות

phrases.english: In what case did you set it up?
Where there is not an olive-bulk.
If so,
in the case of sacrificial animals, why does it make things impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ? דְּלֵיכָּא כְּזַיִת. אִי הָכִי

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 8 that the משנה means a bone with less than a כזית of marrow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טומאה of a bone of מוקדשים depends on there being פיגול or נותר, which needs a כזית. With less than a כזית, the bone should not make anyone טמא.

steps.title: Then why does a perforated bone of a נבלה or a שרץ make things טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second challenge: if there is less than a כזית of marrow, why do the thigh bones of a נבלה and a שרץ make things טמא once they have a hole?
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: the thigh bone of a נבלה and the thigh bone of a שרץ, when they have a hole, why do they make things טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem for the 'less than a כזית' answer. This one comes from the משנה's rule about a נבלה and a שרץ in Step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these bones make things טמא only when they have a hole. A hole matters only because it gives access to the marrow inside. If the marrow is less than the amount needed, then a hole should not change anything, so why are perforated bones טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, used to add another challenge
Thigh bone
They have a hole

phrases.english: And furthermore,

when they were perforated,

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 8 that the משנה means a bone with less than a כזית of marrow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hole makes the bone טמא only because of the marrow inside. If there is not enough marrow, the hole should make no difference.

steps.title: The first clause has less than a כזית, the later clause has a full כזית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenges about מוקדשים and נבלה by saying the משנה's two clauses describe different amounts of marrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not a problem. The first part of the משנה is talking about a bone with less than a כזית of marrow. The later part is talking about a bone with a full כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the questions from steps 11 and 12. It says the two halves of the משנה are talking about different bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained the whole משנה as a bone with less than a כזית of marrow, and that did not fit the clauses about מוקדשים and נבלה. Now only the first clause, the thigh bone of a corpse, is about less than a כזית. The later clause is about a full כזית, so those animals' bones can make things טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult; this introduces an answer
The first clause of the משנה
The later or final clause of the משנה
An olive's volume, the minimum amount for many laws

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the whole משנה now has a full כזית. Only the later clause does. The first clause, about a corpse's bone, still has less than a כזית.

phrases.english: That is not difficult,
the first clause is where there is not an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the thigh bone of a corpse. The amount is the marrow inside it.

phrases.english: the later clause is where there is an olive-bulk.

steps.terutzMaskana: Only the first clause has less than a כזית. The later clause has a full כזית.

steps.title: What new lesson is the משנה teaching?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the later clause has a full כזית, the גמרא asks what the משנה is teaching us that we did not already know.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the משנה teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next few steps. If the bones have a full כזית, why does the משנה need to tell us anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full כזית of forbidden or טמא food obviously counts. So once the later clause has a full כזית, its rulings look obvious. The גמרא wants to know what the new lesson is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? This asks for the new lesson

phrases.english: And what is he teaching us?

steps.title: Several separate lessons, starting with the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches several separate lessons. The first clause teaches that marrow inside a bone does not heal the flesh outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us several different things. The first clause teaches us that marrow inside the bone does not heal the flesh outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each clause of the משנה has its own lesson. It starts with the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, the corpse's thigh bone with less than a כזית of marrow, teaches that the marrow does not make the bone count as a full limb. This is the same idea רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא drew in step 10.

steps.title: The lesson of the מוקדשים clause: a bone that holds נותר
steps.stepSummary: The מוקדשים clause teaches that a bone that holds נותר counts, as רבי יצחק said: such bones make hands טמא because they became a base for something forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the מוקדשים clause teach us? That a bone serving נותר counts. As מרי בר אבוה said in the name of רבי יצחק: bones of קדשים that held נותר make the hands טמא, because they became a base for a forbidden thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second lesson, from the clause about מוקדשים. It supports the point with a statement of רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נותר is meat of a קרבן left past its time, and it makes hands טמא. The new idea is that the bone holding the נותר is treated the same way. This is because it became a בסיס, a base, for the forbidden thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of a קרבן left after the time it may be eaten
Make the hands טמא
A base for a forbidden thing; it gets treated like that thing
Sacrificial animals

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of בסיס, that a base takes on the status of what rests on it, appears in other areas of הלכה too.

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals, what is he teaching us?
That something serving notar is significant,
phrases.notes: He means the bone that holds the leftover meat or marrow counts as something important.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָרִי בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: as Mari bar Avuh said that Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
Bones of sacrificial animals that served notar
make the hands impure,
since they became a base
for a forbidden thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of lessons, moving to the מוקדשים clause
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bone that holds נותר counts and makes the hands טמא, because it became a base for something forbidden.

steps.title: The lesson of the נבלה clause: only a perforated bone
steps.stepSummary: The נבלה clause teaches that even with a full כזית of marrow, the bone makes things טמא only if it has a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a נבלה, even though there is a כזית, if the bone has a hole, yes, it makes things טמא. If it has no hole, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third lesson, from the clause about נבלה. A full כזית of marrow is not enough by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers step 12. The bone has a full כזית, which explains why it can make things טמא at all. The new lesson is that this happens only when the bone is perforated, not when it is sealed.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
It was perforated; it has a hole
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: With a full כזית, each later clause still has its own lesson: a bone holding נותר counts as a base, and a נבלה bone makes things טמא only when it has a hole.

phrases.aramaic: נְבֵלָה, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: An unslaughtered carcass, even though there is an olive-bulk,
if it was perforated, yes,
if it was not perforated, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְבֵלָה, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of lessons with the נבלה clause
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even with a full כזית, a נבלה's bone makes things טמא only if it was perforated.

steps.title: אביי: marrow does heal, but the bone was scraped
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees: marrow inside does heal the flesh outside. The משנה is talking about a bone that was scraped.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, marrow inside does heal the flesh outside. But here we are dealing with a case where the bone was scraped.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different answer to the challenge in step 9. He does not accept the conclusion of step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked: if marrow can heal the flesh outside, the bone should count as a limb and make things טמא through אהל. Step 10 answered that marrow does not heal. אביי says marrow does heal, but in the משנה's case the bone was scraped, so the flesh cannot grow back, and the bone does not count as a full limb.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually; really. Used to bring back an idea that was set aside
Here what are we dealing with? This introduces a specific case
That he scraped it

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say the marrow never heals. He agrees it heals, and he explains the משנה as a special case where the bone was scraped.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא says marrow does not heal the flesh outside. אביי says it does heal, but the משנה is about a scraped bone.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Actually, marrow on the inside
does heal the flesh on the outside,
and here, what are we dealing with?
Where he scraped it.
phrases.notes: Once the bone is scraped, the flesh cannot grow back, so it does not count as a full limb for אהל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם מוֹחַ מִבִּפְנִים מַעֲלֶה אֲרוּכָה מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the challenge of step 9 and answers it differently from step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the bone does not make things טמא through אהל, the marrow must not heal the flesh outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The marrow does heal, but the משנה is about a scraped bone, which cannot regrow its flesh.

steps.title: אביי's reading fits רבי אלעזר's rule about a scraped thigh bone
steps.stepSummary: אביי's scraped-bone reading of the משנה matches רבי אלעזר: a thigh bone scraped lengthwise is still טמא, but one scraped widthwise is pure. The memory sign is a palm tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this fits רבי אלעזר, who said: A thigh bone that was scraped along its length is טמא. One scraped across its width is pure. Your memory sign is a palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's reading by pointing to רבי אלעזר's rule about scraped bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the משנה is talking about a scraped bone that can no longer heal, so it is not a full limb and does not make things טמא through אהל. רבי אלעזר's rule shows that scraping can do this. A bone scraped lengthwise can still heal and stays a limb (טמאה), but a bone scraped widthwise cannot heal, so it is not treated as a limb (טהורה).

keyTerms.meaning: A thigh bone (a long, hollow bone with marrow inside)
He scraped it (shaved off its outer surface)
Along its length / across its width
Your memory sign (a hint to help you remember a rule)
A palm tree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the directions. Scraped LENGTHWISE means טמא, because it can still heal. Scraped WIDTHWISE means pure, because it cannot heal.

phrases.english: And this is like Rabbi Elazar,
as Rabbi Elazar said:
A thigh bone that one scraped lengthwise is impure;
if widthwise, it is pure.
And your memory sign: a palm tree.
phrases.notes: A palm tree cut along its length can recover, but cut all the way around it cannot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by citing רבי אלעזר's rule that a scraped bone (widthwise) cannot heal and loses its status as a limb.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the משנה is talking about a scraped bone that cannot heal, so it is not a full limb and does not make things טמא through אהל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's rule: a thigh bone scraped lengthwise is טמא, but one scraped widthwise is pure

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: marrow heals, and 'touching' includes overhanging
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the משנה differently. There really is a full כזית of marrow, and it does heal the outside. So the bone is also טמא through overhanging (אוהל), and the משנה's word 'touching' includes overhanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Really there is a כזית of marrow, and marrow inside does heal the outside. And what does the משנה mean when it says 'touching'? It also means overhanging.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different way to read the משנה from אביי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי agreed that marrow heals, but he needed a scraped bone so that the bone would not be a full limb that makes things טמא by אוהל. רבי יוחנן does not need that special case: there is a full כזית of marrow, it heals, and the bone really does make things טמא by אוהל. So he reads the משנה's word 'touching' (נוגע) as including overhanging (מאהיל).

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (the case is just as we first thought)
Heals, makes the flesh outside the bone grow back
Touches
Overhangs (is under the same roof or covering as the טומאה, called אוהל)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Actually, there is an olive-size of marrow,
and marrow on the inside
does heal the outside.
And what is the 'touching' that it teaches? Overhanging as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's scraped-bone reading and keeps the plain case of a full כזית of marrow.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה (נוגע also includes מאהיל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If marrow heals, the משנה should have said the bone is טמא by אוהל, not only by touching
steps.terutzMaskana: Marrow does heal, the bone is טמא by אוהל, and 'touching' in the משנה covers overhanging too

steps.title: Then why is a closed נבלה or שרץ bone pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: if marrow inside heals the outside, why does the משנה say a נבלה or שרץ thigh bone without a hole is pure?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if marrow inside heals the outside, why are a נבלה thigh bone and a שרץ thigh bone pure when they have no hole?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's idea using the משנה's second clause about נבלה and שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the marrow 'heals' the bone and makes it count as covered with flesh, then touching the outside should be like touching the marrow itself. Yet the משנה says a closed נבלה or שרץ bone is pure. That seems to show marrow does not heal.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
A small creeping creature whose body is טמא
They were pierced (have a hole)

phrases.english: But if marrow on the inside
heals the outside,
the thigh bone of a carcass and the thigh bone of a creeping creature,
when they were not pierced, why are they pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מוֹחַ מִבִּפְנִים מַעֲלֶה אֲרוּכָה מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's claim from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that marrow inside heals the outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If marrow heals, a closed נבלה or שרץ bone should be טמא by touch, but the משנה says it is pure

steps.title: The case is loose, rattling marrow
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנימין בר גידל answers in רבי יוחנן's name: the משנה is talking about a כזית of marrow that is loose and rattling. For a מת, the טומאה bursts upward anyway. For a נבלה, loose marrow cannot heal, so the bone is טמא only if it has a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנימין בר גידל said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Here we are dealing with a case where there is a כזית of marrow that rattles around. For a מת, the טומאה bursts out and goes up. For a נבלה, since the marrow rattles, if the bone has a hole it is טמא, and if not, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by narrowing the משנה to a special case of loose marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose, rattling marrow is not attached to the bone, so it does not 'heal' it. That is why a closed נבלה bone stays pure. A מת is different, because its טומאה bursts out and rises no matter what, so even a closed bone makes things טמא by אוהל.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrower case)
Rattling (loose and not attached)
The טומאה bursts out and rises upward (a rule special to a מת)
Yes / no

steps.whatToRemember: Two readings of the משנה: אביי says it is a scraped bone. רבי יוחנן says marrow does heal, so the bone is טמא by אוהל too. The נבלה clause is about loose, rattling marrow, which cannot heal, so it is טמא only with a hole. A מת's טומאה bursts upward regardless.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key difference between the טומאה of a מת and the טומאה of a נבלה. A מת's טומאה pushes through barriers, but a נבלה's טומאה needs real contact.

phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Giddel said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where there is an olive-size of marrow that rattles,
with a corpse, the impurity bursts out and rises;
with a carcass, since it is rattling,
phrases.notes: Loose marrow can't 'heal' the bone, so the outside does not count as touching the marrow.

phrases.english: if it was pierced, yes; if it was not pierced, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן): the marrow is loose and rattling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marrow always heals, so a closed נבלה bone should be טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: Loose marrow does not heal. A closed נבלה bone is pure, while a מת's טומאה bursts upward anyway

steps.title: A משנה where touching and overhanging join together
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין (or רבי יוסי בר אבין) quotes a משנה: a person who touches half a כזית of a מת and overhangs another half a כזית (or has half a כזית over him) is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said (some say it was רבי יוסי בר אבין): We also learned this in a משנה. Someone who touches half an olive-size piece of a dead body, and also overhangs another half olive-size piece, or a half olive-size piece is over him, is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support רבי יוחנן's idea that overhanging can be called 'touching'. Right now it only quotes the case. The next step explains why this case proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you need a full כזית of a מת to become טמא. Here the person has only half a כזית by touching and half a כזית by overhanging, and he is still טמא. So the two halves must combine into one full measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching. Becoming טמא through physical contact.
Overhanging. Being over the טומאה, or having it over you, like a tent.
Half an olive-size. Only half of the amount needed to make someone טמא.
Ritually impure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said, and some say it was Rabbi Yosei bar Avin:
We too have learned this in a Mishnah –
One who touches about half an olive-bulk of a corpse,
and overhangs another half olive-bulk,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חֲצִי זַיִת מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו – טָמֵא.
phrases.english: or half an olive-bulk overhangs him – he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's claim (step 20) that the משנה's word 'touching' includes overhanging.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that touching and overhanging are treated as the same thing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה אהלות 3:1, where a half כזית touched and a half כזית overhung join together to make a person טמא.

steps.title: Halves only join if they are one type of impurity
steps.stepSummary: Halves can join only if touching and overhanging are 'one name' (one type). The same משנה states the rule that two different types do not join. So touching and overhanging must be one type.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say touching and overhanging are one type, that is why the halves join. But if you say they are two types, how could they join? We learned: this is the rule: whatever is from one type joins and makes you טמא. If it is from two types, you stay טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה proves the point. Halves of טומאה join only when they are the same kind, so touching and overhanging must be one kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself gives a general rule: half-measures of the same type combine, and half-measures of different types do not. Since touching plus overhanging does combine, the two are one type. That fits רבי יוחנן's use of the word 'touching' to include overhanging.

keyTerms.meaning: One 'name'. One category or type of טומאה.
Two 'names'. Two separate categories of טומאה.
Joins together. Two small amounts combine into one full measure.
This is the general rule.
Ritually pure.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of the proof. The rule about joining depends on the type of טומאה, and that is how the גמרא learns that touching and overhanging are one category.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חַד שְׁמָא הוּא –
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is one category –
that is why they join together.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ תְּרֵי שְׁמֵי נִינְהוּ –
phrases.english: But if you say they are two categories –
would they join together?
But we learned: This is the principle:
phrases.notes: This rule is in the same משנה in אהלות.

phrases.english: anything that is of one category –
joins together and is impure;
of two categories – it is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חַד שְׁמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the proof quoted in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: Touching and overhanging are one category, so 'touching' can include overhanging.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general rule in משנה אהלות 3:1: only halves of the same category join together.

steps.title: Pushing back with the next clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: are they really one category? It starts quoting the סיפא of the same משנה, beginning 'But…'. The quote continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, is it really one category? Say the end part of the משנה: 'But…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to the proof. It is setting up a quote from the end of the same משנה, and the quote continues beyond this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on touching and overhanging being one category. The גמרא now signals that the סיפא of that same משנה seems to treat them as two categories. That would undo the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what?' This opens a challenge to the idea just said.
The last clause or ending part of a משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished here. The words after 'אבל' continue past this point, so don't look for the full objection yet.

phrases.english: Rather, what – is it one category?
Say the latter clause: But

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי חַד שְׁמָא הוּא? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from step 24 by turning to the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that touching and overhanging are one category.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא of the same משנה (still being quoted) seems to treat touching and overhanging as separate categories. That would contradict the proof.
